ml-cluster-kmeans-07: k-means++ ka second seed random hai par weighted: jo point chosen seed 4 se jitna door, utna zyada chance. Weight distance hai ya kuch aur?
Rule: $P(x) = D(x)^2 / \sum D^2$, jahan $D(x)$ = seed 4 se distance. Seed 4 ka apna weight 0 hai.
Point 1 ka $D^2 = 9$, point 6 ka $D^2 = 4$. Ab 9 aur 13 ke $D^2$ nikaal kar total banao. Trap: plain $D$ se weight dena.
ml-cluster-kmeans-08: Do seeds (0 aur 10) pehle se chune hain. Har baaki point ka weight uske **nearest** seed ki distance se banta hai, sirf pehle seed se nahi.
Point 9: nearest seed 10, $D = 1$, $D^2 = 1$. Ab 2 aur 5 ke $D^2$ nikaalo. Trap: 9 ki distance 0 se (81) le lena.
ml-cluster-kmeans-09: Update step sirf cluster ka centre nikaalta hai. Kaun sa centre — mean ya median? Aur cluster me kitne points hain?
$\mu_1 = \frac{1}{4}\sum x_i$, coordinate-wise: x ka mean aur y ka mean alag-alag.
x-coordinates ka sum $0+2+1+5 = 8$. Ab 4 se divide karo, phir y ke liye same karo. Trap: $(0,0)$ ko ginti se bahar kar dena.
ml-cluster-kmeans-10: 'Until the assignments stop changing' — ek iteration par mat ruko. Har iteration: nearest centroid (1D me midpoint boundary), phir mean.
Iter 1 ki boundary $(0+3)/2 = 1.5$. Update ke baad nayi boundary = naye centroids ka midpoint; SSE final centroids se, squared.
Iter 1 ke baad $c_1 = 0$, $c_2 = 46/5 = 9.2$, boundary 4.6. Ab 3 aur 4 kidhar jaate hain, dekh kar dobara update karo. Trap: iter 1 par SSE nikaal dena.
ml-cluster-kmeans-11: Har option alag fact check karta hai: $J$ ka minimum, do centroids ki boundary ka shape, convergence ka rule, aur distance squared hai ya nahi.
Option B: $\lVert x-\mu_1\rVert^2 = \lVert x-\mu_2\rVert^2$ expand karo, $x^Tx$ cancel hota hai. Option C: assignment same → mean same → phir kya?
Option A: $k = n$ pe har point khud centroid hai, $\lVert x - x\rVert^2$ kitna? Trap: option D me formula ka exponent dhyan se dekho.
ml-cluster-kmeans-12: Socho: $k$ badhane se optimal SSE upar jaata hai ya neeche? $k = 200$ (har point apna centroid) pe SSE kitna hoga?
Rule: optimal SSE $k$ ke saath non-increasing hai. To 'smallest SSE' hamesha range ke kis end par milega?
$k = n = 200$ pe SSE $= 0$, aur beech me bhi girta hi rehta hai. Ab option padho jo ye trend aur iska ilaaj bataye. Trap: direction ulta padhna.
ml-cluster-kmeans-13: SSE ke liye pehle har cluster ka centroid (mean) chahiye, phir har point ka **squared** distance apne hi centroid se.
Cluster 1 mean $= ((1+3+2)/3, (1+1+4)/3)$, cluster 2 mean $= (7, 5)$. Har point ka term $\Delta x^2 + \Delta y^2$.
Cluster 2: $(6,5)$ aur $(8,5)$ dono centroid se 1 door, contribution 2. Ab cluster 1 ke teen terms jodo. Trap: square root wali distance jodna.
ml-cluster-kmeans-14: Dono runs ko alag-alag convergence tak trace karna hai. Start alag hai, to final clusters bhi alag ho sakte hain.
1D me assignment boundary = do centroids ka midpoint. Run A ki pehli boundary 15, Run B ki 0.5. Har update ke baad boundary dobara nikaalo.
Run B iter 1: {0} aur baaki sab, $c_2 = 54/5 = 10.8$. Ab nayi boundary pe 1 aur 2 kidhar jaate hain? Trap: pehli iteration par ruk jaana.
ml-cluster-kmeans-15: Pehle step me sirf A aur B centres hain. Options A, B pehli iteration ke baare me hain; C, D doosre assignment step ke baare me.
$D(3,3)$: A se $2^2+3^2$, B se $3^2+1^2$ — chhota wala jeetega. Update = cluster ke points ka coordinate-wise mean.
Pehle step ke clusters bana kar naye means nikaalo, phir C aur D dono ke squared distances naye centroids se compare karo. Trap: pehli iteration ko hi convergence maan lena.
ml-cluster-kmeans-16: Convergence tak trace karna hai. Notice: 100 baaki points se bahut door hai — wo jis cluster me hoga, uska mean kheench lega.
1D me boundary $= (c_1 + c_2)/2$. Iter 1 ki boundary 3.5; phir dono clusters ke means nikaalo.
Iter 1 ke baad $c_2 = (4+5+6+100)/4 = 28.75$. Nayi boundary nikaal kar dekho 4, 5, 6 kidhar jaate hain. Trap: ek iteration par ruk jaana.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-06: Coordinates nahi hain, sirf dissimilarities. Medoid ki definition yaad karo: kis cheez ka minimum chahiye?
Medoid = wo object jiski baaki sab se total dissimilarity sabse kam ho, yaani matrix ki **poori row** ka sum.
P ki row: $1 + 4 + 6 + 7 = 18$. Baaki chaar rows bhi isi tarah jodo. Trap: sirf diagonal ke right wali entries jodna.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-07: Medoid (ek point) aur uska total cost (ek number) alag cheezein hain. Yahan cost poochha hai.
1D + absolute distance: medoid = median data point. Phir cost $= \sum |x - m|$ paanchon points par.
Sorted data ka beech wala point lo. 42 wala term bada hoga, use bhi jodna hai. Trap: mean 15 se distances jodna.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-08: Sirf medoid 2 badalna hai; 16 fixed hai. Har candidate ke baad **har point** ko naye nearest medoid se jodna hai.
Cost $= \sum_x \min(|x - m|, |x - 16|)$ with $m \in \{3, 6, 7, 9, 18\}$. Sabse chhota total chahiye.
$m = 3$: costs $1, 0, 3, 4, 6, 0, 2$, total 16. Baaki candidates bhi isi tarah. Trap: swap se pehle wala cost likh dena.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-09: PAM har (medoid, non-medoid) swap ka naya total cost dekhta hai aur sabse kam wala chunta hai. Notice: kaun sa medoid (3 ya 30) apne points se door baitha hai?
Cost $= \sum_x \min(|x - m_1|, |x - m_2|)$. Swap ke baad har point ko dobara nearest medoid do.
{3, 17} try karo: $2+0+1+5+3+2+0+13 = 26$. Ab baaki options ke medoid sets bhi isi tarah. Trap: mean ke paas wala point chun lena.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-10: Har option k-medoids ki ek property check karta hai: 1D me medoid, cost ka form, kaisa data chalega, aur optimality.
Yaad rakho: cost $= \sum d(x, \text{medoid})$, unsquared; centre hamesha ek data point; sirf dissimilarity chahiye.
Option A check: $\{1, 2, 10\}$ me $m = 2$ ka cost $1 + 0 + 8 = 9$, $m = 1$ ka 10. Baaki options isi rule se jaancho. Trap: PAM ko global optimum maan lena.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-11: Distance Manhattan hai, Euclidean nahi. $C(5,0)$ jaise point pe dono distances alag medoid chun sakti hain — dhyan se.
Har point ka cost $= \min(|x| + |y|,\ |x-3| + |y-4|)$; medoids A aur D ka apna cost 0.
B: A se $1+2 = 3$, D se $2+2 = 4$, to B ka cost 3. Ab C, E, F karo. Trap: C ko aankh se D ke paas maan lena.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-12: Ek hi value badli hai, par bahut zyada. Mean aur medoid dono naye data $\{2,4,6,8,200\}$ par alag-alag nikaalo.
Mean $= \sum x/5$. Medoid = wo data point jiska $\sum |x - m|$ sabse kam ho (1D me median point).
$m = 6$ ka total: $4 + 2 + 0 + 2 + 194 = 202$. Ab $m = 8$ ka total aur naya mean nikaalo. Trap: mean ke paas wala point medoid maan lena.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-13: Swap ke baad medoids {A, E} hain. **Har** non-medoid ko dobara nearest medoid do — sirf D wale points ko nahi.
Cost $= \sum_x \min(d(x, A), d(x, E))$ over B, C, D, F; table ke A aur E columns padho.
B: $\min(2, 4) = 2$; D: $\min(7, 3) = 3$. Ab C aur F. Trap: C ko purane medoid A ke saath hi chhod dena.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-14: Swap = ek current medoid ko ek current non-medoid se badalna. Kitne medoids hain aur kitne non-medoids?
Non-medoids $= 20 - 4 = 16$. Ab multiply karo. Trap: saare pairs $\binom{20}{2}$ gin lena.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-15: PAM ek greedy local search hai: ek baar me ek swap, aur sirf tab jab total cost ghate. Har option ko isi rule se jaancho.
Swap ke baad assignment poora dobara hota hai: har point apne nearest medoid ko. Accept rule: naya total < purana total.
Option A: swap sirf cost ghatne par accept hota hai — to cost kabhi badh sakti hai? Trap: sochna ki sirf hataaye gaye medoid ke points hi hilte hain.
ml-cluster-kmedoids-16: Medoid ek data point hi hoga, aur Manhattan distances ke **total** se chuna jaata hai — mean ke paas hona zaroori nahi.
Har point ke liye $\sum (|\Delta x| + |\Delta y|)$ baaki chaar points tak. Sabse chhota total jeetega.
S ka total: P 3, Q 2, R 6, T 5, yaani 16. Ab Q aur T ke totals nikaal kar compare karo. Trap: mean ke sabse paas wala point chunna.
ml-cluster-linkage-07: Average linkage me saare cross pairs (ek point X se, ek Y se) ka mean lena hai — centroids ki distance nahi.
Pehle do pairs: $|1-4| = 3$, $|1-12| = 11$. Baaki do pairs 7 se nikaalo. Trap: centroids 4 aur 8 ki distance le lena.
ml-cluster-linkage-08: Single linkage: do clusters ki distance = sabse paas wala cross pair. Har step me current table ka minimum merge hota hai.
Update: $d(X\cup Y, Z) = \min(d(X,Z), d(Y,Z))$. Shuru matrix ki chhoti entries D–E aur A–B se karo.
D–E (2) aur A–B (3) merge. Ab $d(C, \{A,B\}) = \min(7, 4) = 4$ aur $d(C, \{D,E\}) = \min(6, 5) = 5$. Aage trace karo. Trap: complete ka max lena.
ml-cluster-linkage-09: Complete linkage: cluster distance = sabse **door** wala cross pair. Phir sab cluster-pairs me se **sabse chhoti** distance wala merge hota hai.
Teen clusters bache: {P}, {R}, {Q,S,T}. Teen distances chahiye: P–R, P–{Q,S,T}, R–{Q,S,T}.
$d(P, \{Q,S,T\}) = \max(10, 9, 12) = 12$. Ab R–{Q,S,T} aur P–R nikaal kar sabse chhota chuno. Trap: R ka nearest member (single rule) dekhna.
ml-cluster-linkage-10: Average linkage = clusters ke **saare point pairs** ka mean. Sizes alag hon to sub-cluster distances ka seedha average galat ho sakta hai.
$d(X, Y) = \frac{1}{|X||Y|}\sum d(x, y)$. Pehla merge matrix ki sabse chhoti entry C–D = 3.
Ab $d(B, \{C,D\}) = (4+7)/2 = 5.5$; ise B–E $= 6$ aur baaki se compare karo, phir aage trace. Trap: last step me do sub-cluster distances ka seedha average.
ml-cluster-linkage-11: Har option alag linkage ka hai. Pehle matrix ki sabse chhoti entry dekho — kya pehla merge linkage par depend karta hai?
Rules: single = min, complete = max, average = saare pairs ka mean. C ke liye {A,B} aur {D,E} dono se distance nikaalo.
Complete: $d(C, \{D,E\}) = \max(9, 5) = 9$. Ab $d(C, \{A,B\})$ nikaal kar compare karo. Trap: option D me sirf ek side (C–{A,B}) dekhna.
ml-cluster-linkage-12: UPGMA me har **point pair** barabar gina jaata hai. B ke 3 points hain, A ka sirf 1 — to dono distances ka weight same nahi.
Numerator: $1\cdot4 + 3\cdot8$. Ab sizes ke sum se divide karo. Trap: $(4+8)/2$ wala seedha average.
ml-cluster-linkage-13: Complete linkage = farthest cross pair. Distance Manhattan hai: $|\Delta x| + |\Delta y|$, Euclidean nahi.
Chaar cross pairs banao: X ka har point Y ke har point se. Inme sabse **bada** chahiye.
$(1,2)$ se $(5,2)$: $4 + 0 = 4$; $(1,2)$ se $(4,4)$: $3 + 2 = 5$. Ab $(0,0)$ wale do pairs. Trap: Euclidean distance lagana.
ml-cluster-linkage-14: Socho kaunse clusters badle: sirf A aur B jud gaye. Baaki clusters ke points wahi ke wahi hain.
Do untouched clusters C aur D ki distance sirf unke apne points par depend karti hai. To kaunsi entries badlengi?
Example: {1}, {2}, {9}, {10} me {1} aur {2} merge hue. Kya $d(\{9\}, \{10\}) = 1$ badla? Trap: poori table dobara banana.
ml-cluster-linkage-15: Pehle chhote gaps se do pairs banenge. Phir complete linkage me cluster distance = dono clusters ke sabse door wale do points.
Pehle merges {2,3} aur {7,9}. Ab teen distances compare karo: {2,3}–{7,9}, {7,9}–15, {2,3}–15, har ek ka farthest pair.
$d(\{7,9\}, 15) = 15 - 7 = 8$. Ab $d(\{2,3\}, \{7,9\})$ nikaal kar compare karo. Trap: nearest gap $7 - 3$ (single rule) lena.
ml-cluster-linkage-16: Har option ek linkage property hai. Chhote examples se test karo: do singletons, ya 1D ke do chhote clusters.
Single = min, complete = max, average = mean — sab cross pairs $d(x, y)$ par. Max ke set me naye pairs judein to max kya kar sakta hai?
Option B test: $X = \{0, 2\}$, $Y = \{1, 3\}$ — cross pairs ka mean aur centroids 1, 2 ki distance compare karo. Trap: option D me max ko ghatta hua maan lena.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-07: Har horizontal bar ek merge hai; uski height axis se padho. 3 clusters ke liye cut ke neeche kitne merges chahiye?
Clusters $= 6 - \#\{\text{merges at height} \le h\}$. 3 clusters ⇒ cut ke neeche exactly 3 merges.
Heights sorted likho: sabse neeche A–B (1), phir E–F. Teesra aur chautha merge kis height par hai? Trap: range ka upper end galat lena.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-08: Leaves ka left-right order cluster nahi batata; sirf bars ki heights batati hain. Height 2.5 par ek horizontal line socho.
Jo merges height ≤ 2.5 par hain, sirf wahi hue. Clusters $= 5 - (\text{aise merges})$.
A–E ka bar height 1 par hai, cut ke neeche. Ab B–D aur C wale bars ki height padho. Trap: paas-paas drawn leaves ko ek cluster maan lena.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-09: Har merge clusters ki ginti 1 se ghatata hai. Shuru me kitne clusters the aur cut ke baad kitne bache?
Clusters $= n - (\text{merges below the cut})$, with $n = 15$ and clusters $= 4$.
Total merges $= 15 - 1 = 14$, par poochha hai sirf cut ke **neeche** wale. Trap: cut ke upar wale merges gin lena.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-10: Single-linkage merge heights = MST ki edge weights. 1D me MST sirf padosi (sorted order me agle) points ko jodta hai.
Sorted points ke consecutive gaps nikaalo: $4-3$, $8-4$, $15-8$, … Ye hi merge heights hain, kisi bhi order me.
Gaps 1, 4, 7 mil gaye; baaki do gaps bhi nikaal kar sab jodo. Trap: complete linkage ki heights lena, ya sirf last merge height.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-11: Figure se teen merge heights padho. Phir har linkage se ye heights khud nikaal kar match karo.
Pehla merge {2,3} har linkage me 1 par. Doosra: 0 ka {2,3} se distance — single = min(2, 3), complete = max(2, 3), average = mean.
Single me 0 height $\min(2,3) = 2$ par judta. Baaki linkages ki doosri aur teesri heights nikaal kar figure se milao. Trap: single aur complete swap kar dena.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-12: Har option dendrogram cut ki ek general property hai. Chhote data (jaise 0, 1, 3) par soch kar test karo.
Cut rule: clusters $= n - \#\{\text{merges} \le h\}$. h badhao to ye count kis taraf jaata hai? Aur merges kabhi tootte nahi.
Option B: 0, 1, 3 par single ki heights 1, 2 aur complete ki 1, 3. Cut 2.5 par dono me clusters gino. Trap: option D me tied heights bhool jaana.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-13: Pehle complete-linkage merges aur unki heights trace karo, phir cut 7.5 ke neeche wale merges gino.
Complete update: $d(X\cup Y, Z) = \max(d(X,Z), d(Y,Z))$. Clusters $= 5 - \#\{\text{merges} \le 7.5\}$.
Pehla merge R–T at 3. Ab $d(Q, \{R,T\}) = \max(8, 5) = 8$; ise P–S aur Q–S se compare karo. Trap: single linkage ka min lena.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-14: Dendrogram me leaves ka left-right order sirf drawing hai. Asli information bars ki heights me hai.
Do leaves kab ek cluster me aate hain? Jab cut un dono ko jodne wale sabse neeche ke bar ke upar ya barabar ho.
Cut 5 par X–Y ka joint (6) cut ke upar hai — saath ya alag? Ab cut 7 socho. Trap: paas drawn leaves ko closest pair maan lena.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-15: Tied height par ek hi cut do merges ek saath paar karta hai, to clusters 2 se girte hain. Kaun se k chhoot jaate hain?
Clusters $= 7 - \#\{\text{merges} \le h\}$. h ko 0 se upar le jao aur har interval ka count likho.
$h < 1$: 7 clusters; $1 \le h < 2$: dono height-1 merges ho gaye, to 5. Aage ke intervals bhi likho. Trap: maan lena ki 1 se 7 tak har k milta hai.
ml-cluster-dendrogram-16: Figure se har bar ki height padho: kaun kis height par juda. Phir har option ka cut alag se check karo.
Cut h: clusters $= 7 - \#\{\text{merges} \le h\}$; do leaves saath tab hain jab unka joint $\le h$ ho.
Q–R ka joint 1 par, U–V ka 2 par. Option A ke liye 3.5 ke neeche kitne bars hain, gino. Trap: leaves (7) ko merges ki ginti maan lena.
